description: Turns CV and gates into MIDI for an external device, with each note number worked out from the tuning held by an MTS-ESP master

inputs.text: The pitch at 1V per octave; the note number comes from the MTS-ESP tuning when a master is connected, and its channel count sets how many notes are sent
A note sounds on that channel while this is at 1V or above, and ends when it falls
Sets the velocity of the note on that channel, 0 to 10V across the MIDI range of 0 to 127; with nothing patched it counts as 100
Sets the key pressure sent for the note on that channel, 0 to 10V across the MIDI range of 0 to 127
Sets the pitch wheel, ±5V across its full fourteen-bit range
Sets the mod wheel, 0 to 10V across the MIDI range of 0 to 127
A MIDI clock pulse is sent while this is at 1V or above
Sets the channel volume controller, 0 to 10V across the MIDI range of 0 to 127; with nothing patched it counts as 10V
Sets the pan controller, ±5V across the MIDI range of 0 to 127
A MIDI start message is sent while this is at 1V or above
A MIDI stop message is sent while this is at 1V or above
A MIDI continue message is sent while this is at 1V or above

notes: nothing is sent until a driver, a device and a channel have been chosen on the module's own display
with no MTS-ESP master running on the computer the note numbers are worked out as plain twelve-tone tuning; the lamp is fully lit only while a master is found
a master has to be loaded elsewhere: in a VCV Host module in this patch, or in any application on the same computer, since MTS-ESP passes tunings between processes
the two wheel jacks and the volume and pan jacks are read 200 times a second rather than every sample
the driver, device and channel choosers are drawn inside one display widget and cannot be clicked for a help entry of their own
menu: Reset MIDI (Panic) — sends a note off for everything held and resets the MIDI output
